thread:
kim: Cutting release now. Deploy-bot failed manifest verification on canary, holding promotion. :exclamation:

deploy-bot: MANIFEST_VERIFY_FAILED redwood/search-indexer:2026-03-25-canary
  expected sha256: cbf12...
  actual sha256: 9a7e4...
  note: artifact uploaded and HEAD returned 200

dario: that's a checksum mismatch, but upload looked OK. ci-bot, what did the builder compute as the checksum during pipeline?

ci-bot: build/4567 summary:
- pack step: produced artifact search-indexer.tar.gz
- manifest creation: computed checksum as sha256(search-indexer.tar)
- upload: uploaded search-indexer.tar.gz and signed manifest with sha256(search-indexer.tar)
- store shows object key search-indexer.tar.gz
- deploy verification computes sha256 of uploaded object (tar.gz), which does not match manifest (we expected tar)

jen: ahhhh packaging mismatch. Last night the packer image was updated to gzip artifacts in CI (we now produce tar.gz) but manifest generation step wasn't updated and is still hashing the uncompressed tar. So manifest contains sha256(tar) while uploaded object is tar.gz.

dario: options: 1) re-generate manifest with sha256(tar.gz) from the uploaded object and re-sign (fast), 2) rebuild artifact to produce uncompressed tar matching manifest (slower), 3) pin to prior canary and delay. Change window: ~40m.

security-bot: note: re-signing a manifest must be audited. Per release policy we can re-sign when artifact binary hasn't been mutated post-build and CI artifacts are retained with audited logs. This artifact was generated by CI and the content matches the built image; the difference is packaging. If you re-sign, tag the release with audit clause and attach builder logs.

kim: I want minimal risk. Is the binary payload identical? Can we verify container image digest or binary checksums inside tar?

ci-bot: verified: the contained binary checksums (sha256 of /bin/indexer) match between the buildkite artifact and the stored object when we decompress. So only the outer packaging differs. Build logs and signed provenance available at artifact-store/build/4567/prov.json

jen: given that, re-signing is safe and much faster. We'll re-generate manifest using sha256 of the uploaded object and push re-signed manifest. We'll include an audit note referencing the packer image change.

dario: agree. we should also update pack-and-manifest job to compute both tar and tar.gz checksums to avoid this class of break in future. PR queued.

kim: ok proceed with re-sign. jen, can you handle the re-sign and push a minimal release note? I'll hold the cut until deploy-bot confirms verification.

jen: running commands now:
```
aws s3 cp s3://redwood-artifacts/search-indexer/2026-03-25/search-indexer.tar.gz /tmp/
sha256sum /tmp/search-indexer.tar.gz > /tmp/tar_gz.sha256
deployctl sign-manifest --image redwood/search-indexer:2026-03-25-canary --checksum-file /tmp/tar_gz.sha256 --actor jen --reason "packaging format mismatch; artifact correct"
```

deploy-bot: New manifest uploaded. Verifying...

deploy-bot: MANIFEST_VERIFY_OK for redwood/search-indexer:2026-03-25-canary

deploy-bot: Canary rollout resumed -> 5% traffic, smoke tests queued.

kim: great. smoke results?

ci-bot: smoke tests passed (3/3). Observing for 10m per rollout policy.

kim: decision recorded: re-signed manifest due to packer image change. Actions:
- build: update pack-and-manifest job to compute both compressed and uncompressed checksums (PR-7890)
- release: add audit entry linking to prov.json and re-sign event
- ops: add packer image change note to deploy-cheatsheet

security-bot: audit note recorded: re-sign event by jen at 1759012399, provenance attached.

jen: posting short release note: "Canary promoted after manifest re-sign for packaging checksum mismatch; binary content verified. Follow-up CI job updated."

kim: promotion continuing after observation window. Thanks all :rocket:
